# MSG / Email Parser — Usage Guide

*Mode: direct · Works offline*

Parses an Outlook .msg or standard .eml email into structured JSON: sender, date, subject, body text and the list of attachments. Pure deterministic extraction. Works offline and does not use the LLM.

## When to use it

Use this when you need an email's fields as data (for a script, a record, or further processing) rather than reading it in a mail client.

## Inputs

- **Email file (.msg or .eml)** (required) — accepts: Outlook .msg or RFC-822 .eml — one file.
  - The email file to parse.
  - ⚠️ Provide the email file itself; this does not connect to a mailbox.

## How to run

1. Select the .msg or .eml file.
2. Click Run.
3. Download the JSON.

## Output

Output is written to the **`Data/outputs/`** folder, named:

```
Data/outputs/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-email-parsed.json
```

Files produced:

- **`YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-<input>-email-parsed.json`** — Structured JSON with sender, date, subject, body text and an attachments list — easy to read into any script or tool.

## Tips

Attachments are listed (names), so you can see what was enclosed without opening the mail. In a digitally signed .msg the real attachments are unwrapped and listed. An attached email inside a .msg is listed by name but not opened.

## Troubleshooting

| If… | Then… |
|------|-------|
| Body text looks empty. | For .msg files only the plain-text body is read. A .msg that keeps its text only as rich text (RTF) or HTML gives an empty body, and when a rich-text body is present the JSON carries a "warnings" entry saying so; open the original email to read it. .eml files fall back to the HTML body with tags stripped. |
| A signed or encrypted .msg shows no attachments, and the JSON has a "warnings" entry. | The message is opaque-signed S/MIME, so its contents sit inside a sealed envelope that is not opened. Open the original email in Outlook and save the attachments from there. |
| The run stops with "Cannot read ... as an Outlook .msg". | The file is not a real .msg (for example a renamed .eml or a download that was cut short). Re-save or re-download the email and run again. |
